curriculumTitle: How do we use radiation in our lives, and is it safe for humans?
subject: Physics
centralPhenomenon: People using microwave ovens to store electronics and how the oven heats food without an obvious heat source
description: Students investigate electromagnetic radiation through microwave ovens, exploring wave properties, energy transfer, and safety considerations of EM radiation in daily life

parts.partTitle: How does a microwave oven heat up food?
parts.partSubtitle: Investigating wave properties and electromagnetic energy transfer

units.title: Anchoring Phenomenon and Initial Models
units.coreIdea: Microwave ovens heat food without an obvious heat source, raising questions about energy transfer mechanisms.
units.drivingQuestion: How does a microwave oven heat up food without an obvious heat source?
units.phenomenon: Microwave oven heating food and people storing electronics inside ovens
keyContent: Microwave ovens heat food without direct contact heating
Electronics are sometimes stored in microwave ovens
Energy transfer must occur through some mechanism
activities: Observation and questioning about microwave function
units.assessment: Formative: Initial models and question development

units.title: Wave Properties and Relationships
units.coreIdea: Waves have measurable properties including wavelength, frequency, and speed that are mathematically related.
units.drivingQuestion: What are the properties of waves and how are they related?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of wave properties using simulations and physical models
keyContent: Relationship between wavelength, frequency, and speed
Wave properties can be measured and quantified
Mathematical relationships govern wave behavior
units.assessment: Formative: Wave property analysis and relationships

units.title: Production of Electromagnetic Radiation
units.coreIdea: Electromagnetic radiation is produced from electricity using devices like magnetrons, involving moving charged particles.
units.drivingQuestion: How is electromagnetic radiation produced from electricity?
units.phenomenon: Magnetron function and EM radiation generation from electrical sources
keyContent: Moving charged particles create electromagnetic radiation
Magnetrons convert electricity to microwaves
Electric and magnetic fields are interconnected

units.title: Electromagnetic Wave Propagation
units.coreIdea: Moving charged particles create ripples in electric fields that propagate as electromagnetic waves through space.
units.drivingQuestion: How do electromagnetic waves travel through space?
units.phenomenon: Simulations showing electric field ripples and wave propagation
keyContent: Electric field ripples propagate as waves
Electromagnetic waves can travel through empty space
Wave propagation involves energy transfer

units.title: Microwave Containment and Reflection
units.coreIdea: Microwaves are contained within the oven through reflection, providing evidence for wave behavior.
units.drivingQuestion: How are microwaves contained within the oven?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of microwave containment and wave reflection evidence
keyContent: Microwaves reflect off metal surfaces
Oven design contains electromagnetic radiation
Wave reflection is evidence of wave behavior
units.assessment: Formative: Investigation design and evidence analysis

units.title: Material Interactions with Electromagnetic Fields
units.coreIdea: Different materials (water, plastic, metal) interact differently with changing electric fields, explaining heating patterns.
units.drivingQuestion: Why do different materials heat differently in microwaves?
units.phenomenon: Simulation of particle interactions with changing electric fields in different materials
keyContent: Water molecules respond strongly to changing electric fields
Plastic and metal interact differently with EM radiation
Particle-scale interactions explain macroscopic heating
Material structure determines EM interaction
activities: Connection between microscopic and macroscopic effects

units.title: Wave Interference and Hot/Cold Spots
units.coreIdea: Wave interference creates hot and cold spots in microwave ovens due to constructive and destructive interference.
units.drivingQuestion: Why are there hot and cold spots in microwave ovens?
units.phenomenon: Wave interference simulations explaining uneven heating patterns
keyContent: Wave interference creates patterns of high and low intensity
Constructive interference creates hot spots
Destructive interference creates cold spots
Standing wave patterns in enclosed spaces

units.title: Climate Connection - Greenhouse Effect
units.coreIdea: Electromagnetic radiation interactions with matter help explain how greenhouse gases contribute to global temperature rise.
units.drivingQuestion: How do greenhouse gases affect Earth's temperature?
units.phenomenon: Application of EM radiation absorption, reflection, and transmission to climate science
keyContent: Different types of EM radiation interact differently with matter
Greenhouse gases absorb specific wavelengths of radiation
Absorption, reflection, and transmission affect energy balance
Connection between particle interactions and global climate
activities: Greenhouse effect modeling using EM radiation concepts
units.assessment: Formative: Greenhouse effect explanation using EM concepts

parts.partTitle: How do we use electromagnetic radiation safely in our lives?
parts.partSubtitle: Exploring the electromagnetic spectrum and radiation safety

units.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
units.coreIdea: Electromagnetic radiation exists across a spectrum with different wavelengths and frequencies, each with different properties and uses.
units.drivingQuestion: What is the electromagnetic spectrum and how do different types of radiation compare?
units.phenomenon: Building and exploring the complete electromagnetic spectrum
keyContent: EM spectrum ranges from radio waves to gamma rays
Different wavelengths and frequencies have different properties
Scientific notation for comparing magnitudes
Each type of radiation has specific applications
units.assessment: Formative: EM spectrum organization and comparisons

units.title: Wave-Particle Duality and Radiation Models
units.coreIdea: Electromagnetic radiation exhibits both wave and particle (photon) behavior, requiring different models for different phenomena.
units.drivingQuestion: How can electromagnetic radiation be both a wave and a particle?
units.phenomenon: Reading and analysis of wave-particle duality in EM radiation
keyContent: EM radiation can be modeled as waves or photons
Different models are useful for different phenomena
Photon energy is related to frequency
Dual nature is a fundamental property of EM radiation

units.title: Ionizing vs. Non-ionizing Radiation Safety
units.coreIdea: Different types of electromagnetic radiation pose different health risks, with ionizing radiation being more dangerous than non-ionizing radiation.
units.drivingQuestion: Which types of electromagnetic radiation are safe and which are dangerous?
units.phenomenon: Evaluation of radiation safety claims and evidence for different EM radiation types
keyContent: Ionizing radiation can damage cells and DNA
Non-ionizing radiation generally poses lower health risks
Energy levels determine ionization potential
Safety depends on radiation type, intensity, and exposure time
units.assessment: Formative: Radiation safety analysis and evidence evaluation

units.title: Digital Imaging and Information Storage
units.coreIdea: Electromagnetic radiation is used to create and store digital images through technologies like radiography and digital sensors.
units.drivingQuestion: How is electromagnetic radiation used to create and store digital images?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of radiography and digital imaging technologies
keyContent: EM radiation interactions with matter create image contrast
Digital sensors convert radiation to electrical signals
Image information can be stored and processed digitally
Different radiation types provide different imaging capabilities

units.title: Wireless Communication and Binary Code
units.coreIdea: Wireless electronic devices use electromagnetic waves and binary code to enable reliable communication and data transmission.
units.drivingQuestion: How do wireless devices use electromagnetic radiation for communication?
units.phenomenon: Investigation of wireless communication technologies and binary information encoding
keyContent: EM waves carry information through modulation
Binary code enables digital information transmission
Wireless devices encode and decode EM signals
Signal reliability depends on various factors

units.title: Transfer Task - 5G Safety Evaluation
units.coreIdea: Scientific understanding of electromagnetic radiation can be used to evaluate claims about emerging technologies like 5G.
units.drivingQuestion: How can we evaluate claims about 5G radiation safety using our understanding of EM radiation?
units.phenomenon: Evaluation of social media posts about 5G radiation safety using developed EM radiation models
keyContent: Application of EM radiation understanding to evaluate claims
Critical analysis of information sources
Evidence-based reasoning about radiation safety
Communication of scientific understanding to others

disciplinary_core_ideas: PS2.B - Types of Interactions (forces at distance explained by fields)
PS3.A - Definitions of Energy (energy in fields and radiation)
PS4.A - Wave Properties (wavelength, frequency, speed relationships)
PS4.B - Electromagnetic Radiation (waves/photons, thermal conversion, ionizing damage)
PS4.C - Information Technologies (wave-matter interactions for information)
ESS2.D - Weather and Climate (solar radiation and interactions)

focal: Cause and Effect: Mechanism and Explanation
Energy and Matter: Flows, Cycles, and Conservation

key_physics_concepts: Electromagnetic radiation as waves and photons
Wave properties: wavelength, frequency, speed relationships

high_school_physics: Energy transfer and conservation (P.1, P.2, P.3)
Forces at a distance concept (P.4 - if skipped, requires supplemental instruction)
chemistry_biology: Energy stored in magnetic and electric fields

safety_considerations.lab_safety: Specific instructions for PPE and warnings against home microwave investigations
safety_considerations.radiation_sensitivity: Recognition that EM radiation can cause student anxiety
emotional_support: Safe learning culture and classroom discourse
